title: Best Condition Monitoring Systems for Heavy Industry in 2027
summary: Compare 5 condition monitoring systems for crushers, kilns, grinding mills and large motors, with specs and questions to ask before you buy.
body_markdown:
## Key Points


- Match the system to the asset: crushers need shock range, kilns need a slow-speed method, mills need spectral resolution.
- Check hazardous-area certificates before price, since coal mill and fuel handling areas rule out some sensors.
- Compare who reads the data: in-platform AI diagnosis, vendor analysts, or software your own team configures.


For heavy industry, the right condition monitoring system is the one whose sensors fit your worst assets: a cone crusher taking shock loads, a rotary kiln turning slowly in heat, a ball mill with a girth gear, and the large motors that drive them. Generic sensor lists rarely test for those conditions.


This comparison covers five systems that show up in heavy-industry evaluations: Tractian, SKF, Emerson, Augury and Fluke Reliability. It starts with what each asset type demands, then compares specs and the questions to ask before you sign.


## What Should a Heavy-Industry Condition Monitoring System Handle?


A heavy-industry system has to detect faults on high-shock, slow-speed and high-power equipment in dust, heat and sometimes classified areas. That means checking four asset types separately, because a sensor that works on a conveyor motor can miss a kiln support roller.


### Crushers


Jaw, cone and gyratory crushers load their bearings with repeated impacts, so the sensor needs a high acceleration range and a mount that will not shake loose. Dust and washdown water also reach the sensor, so the ingress rating matters as much as the frequency range.


### Rotary kilns


Kiln support rollers and thrust rollers turn slowly, which makes bearing defects hard to see in standard vibration readings. One commenter on Reddit put it plainly when asked about a[low-speed bearing that needed monitoring](https://www.reddit.com/r/IndustrialMaintenance/comments/1llt6uf/does_anyone_have_a_suggestion_for_an_inplace/) : vibration analysis would struggle at that speed and ultrasound was the better choice. The kiln drive gearbox and girth gear still need vibration spectra, and shell heat limits where sensors can sit.


### Grinding mills


Ball, SAG and vertical roller mills fail at the pinion and girth gear mesh, the trunnion bearings and the gearbox. Separating gear mesh frequencies from their sidebands takes a wide frequency range and fine spectral resolution, and lubrication problems on the trunnions show up earlier in ultrasound than in vibration.


### Large motors


Mill drives, induced draft fans and long conveyors run on large motors where mechanical and electrical faults overlap. A magnetic or electrical signal helps tell a rotor bar or stator problem apart from a bearing fault, and RPM tracking matters on variable-frequency drives.


The table below turns those needs into specs you can ask each vendor for.

## 1. Tractian


Best for: Heavy plants that want vibration and ultrasound in one wireless sensor, AI diagnosis of the failure mode, and alerts tied to maintenance work, without building a plant network first.


Tractian is a[condition monitoring platform](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/condition-monitoring) that pairs AI diagnostics with a wireless sensor capturing vibration, ultrasound, temperature and RPM in one device. Smart Trac Ultra samples vibration from 0 to 64 kHz, wide enough for gear mesh on mill drives and impact loading on crusher bearings. Auto Diagnosis then benchmarks each asset's data against millions of historical machine hours and bearing libraries to make an accurate, explainable call, complete with evidence. Sensors are ATEX/IECEx compliant and Class I Div 1 certified, connect over 4G/LTE, and are installed by CMRP/CAT-certified specialists.


### How it diagnoses


[Auto Diagnosis](https://tractian.com/en/resources/videos/auto-diagnosis) maps signal patterns to named failure modes such as bearing wear, misalignment, unbalance, lubrication failure and gear wear, and Energy Trac adds electrical monitoring that flags rotor and stator faults and voltage imbalance on the motor. Each alert carries severity, the evidence behind the call and the next step, ranked by asset criticality.


Each Smart Trac Ultra mounts on one asset and captures vibration and ultrasound in the same sensor, so a slow kiln trunnion bearing gets ultrasound for early friction alongside vibration, with no second device. Tractian's[multimodal monitoring](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/multimodal) goes further, combining that mechanical data with electrical data from Energy Trac on the same asset.


### Deployment in heavy plants


- **Fast setup:** sensors mount with adhesive or drill-and-tap and are up and running in minutes, with no plant wiring.
- **No plant network needed:** sensors talk to Tractian receivers at up to 330 ft through obstacles and 3,300 ft line of sight, and receivers send data over LTE/4G, so remote crushers and quarries stay connected.
- **Hazardous and dirty areas:** Tractian sensors are IP69K sealed and carry[NFPA 70 Class 1, 2, and 3 (Division I) compliance](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/sensor-specifications) , which suits coal mills and fuel handling.
- **Integration:** alerts become work orders in Tractian, and[integrations with CMMS, ERP and EAM systems](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/integrations) such as SAP, Oracle NetSuite and Maximo keep findings in the tools planners already use.


### Customer results in metals


At[Höganäs](https://tractian.com/en/case-studies/hoganas) , Tractian AI detected abnormal vibration on the main hoist motor of the electric arc furnace, which handles more than 33,000 pounds of molten steel. A reliability technician confirmed bearing wear, and the planned repair avoided an unplanned outage and more than $11,000 in potential losses.


Tractian also monitors mining equipment on the surface and underground. Learn more about[mining condition monitoring](https://tractian.com/en/industry/mining-sector) .


### Pricing


Tractian pricing is scoped to the assets in your plant rather than a flat per-sensor list price. A Tractian specialist looks at which crushers, kilns, mills and motors are critical, how each one tends to fail, and how much sensor coverage it takes to catch those failures early, then sends a custom quote built around that risk.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- Does one sensor carry both ultrasound and vibration, so a slow kiln support roller gets both signals without a second device?
- Does each alert name the failure mode, its severity and the next step, or does your team have to read the spectrum first?
- Can the sensors reach the cloud from a quarry or kiln area without plant Wi-Fi or Ethernet?
- Is the sensor Class I Division 1 certified and ATEX/IECEx compliant for areas such as coal mills?


## 2. SKF Enlight Collect IMx-1


**Best for:** Plants that want wireless vibration and temperature monitoring on bearing housings, analyzed remotely by SKF.


### Notable features


The sensor measures vibration and temperature and uses SKF's acceleration enveloping on bearing signals.


- **Network:** sensors form a self-forming mesh, relaying data around pipework and vessels to a gateway.
- **Rating:** the sensor is rated IP69K.
- **Analysis:** data goes to SKF Rotating Equipment Performance centres, where remote analysts interpret it. Tractian also offers human review on top of in-platform AI diagnosis.
- **Range:** the IMx-1 measures acceleration from 10 Hz to 10 kHz.


### Pricing


Contact SKF for a current quote.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- What is the battery life at your sampling rate?
- Who changes the cells, and how many battery changes does your sensor count add each year?
- How do findings from the remote centre reach your planners: as a report, an alarm or a work order in your system?


## 3. Emerson AMS Wireless Vibration Monitor


Best for: Process plants that already run WirelessHART and AMS Machine Works and want wireless vibration data from balance-of-plant and hazardous-area machines in the same software.


### Notable features


The AMS Wireless Vibration Monitor captures triaxial vibration, temperature, speed and PeakVue measurements. PeakVue measures impacting in bearings and gears, and the monitor reports bearing, mechanical and lubrication severity.


- **Data:** 51.2 kHz sampling and spectra up to 1,600 lines, with a 20 kHz main axis.
- **Network:** a WirelessHART mesh with 100 m line-of-sight range, where each sensor relays for its neighbors.
- **Software:** data lands in AMS Machine Works alongside the AMS 6500 ATG and AMS Asset Monitor, with integration to DeltaV and plant historians.
- **Service option:** AMS Machine Works Connect bundles sensors, gateway, cloud software and analysts who review alarms and send diagnostic reports within 24 to 72 hours.


### Pricing


Ask Emerson for current pricing on your asset list.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- What gateway and wiring does a crusher or kiln area need without a WirelessHART network, and who installs it?
- Which certificate covers your coal mill or fuel area?


## 4. Augury


**Best for:** Companies that want machine health monitoring with separate sensor families for standard, ultra-low-speed and hazardous assets, read by AI diagnostics in the Augury platform.


### Notable features


The Halo R4000 reads triaxial vibration, temperature and magnetic flux on motors, pumps, fans and gearboxes, with an IP66/68/69 rating for non-hazardous zones.


- **Slow-speed assets:** the Halo U2000 is an ultrasonic sensor for large gearboxes, rotary drums and kilns, detecting faults down to 1 RPM through a line-powered hub on Wi-Fi or LTE.
- **Hazardous areas:** the Baker Hughes Ranger Pro Gen6 carries Class I Zone 0, ATEX, IECEx and CSA Div 1 approvals and connects over ISA100.11a.
- **Workflow:** alerts feed CMMS and EAM integrations, and supported sensors offer phase analysis for unbalance, misalignment and looseness.


### Pricing


Request a current quote from Augury.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- What type of sensors and gateways are needed, and who installs them?
- How many assets does the year-one budget cover?


## 5. Fluke Reliability Azima Accel 310


Best for: Plants that want wireless triaxial vibration sensors read by Azima AI diagnostics, with Fluke vibration analysts available for second opinions and remote monitoring.


### Notable features


The Accel 310 is the sensor in Fluke Reliability's Watchman AIR system, built on Azima DLI diagnostics. It measures triaxial vibration and surface temperature, sends hourly summary trends, and collects full diagnostic data once a day for automated analysis.


- **Data:** a flat range of 10 to 6,300 Hz with FFT detection to 10.4 kHz, a 26,667 Hz sample rate and 1,600-line spectra.
- **Slow-speed method:** Azima's Impact Demod measurements target bearing faults, covering shafts down to 350 RPM.
- **Hazardous areas and housing:** IP68, ATEX Zone 1 and 2, and US/Canada Class 1 Division 2.
- **Network:** sensors form a 2.4 GHz Wirepas mesh to an Accel gateway that connects over Wi-Fi, Ethernet or cellular LTE-M.
- **Analysis:** WATCHMAN software turns data into fault diagnoses with prioritized repair actions, and Fluke analysts provide human review with a 24-hour turnaround on serious faults.


### Pricing


Reach out to Fluke Reliability for current Watchman AIR pricing.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- What is the lowest shaft speed supported on your kiln support rollers and mill trunnions?
- What input range covers the impact levels on your crusher bearings?
- Does a Class 1 Division 2 rating cover your classified areas, or do some need Division 1 equipment?


## How to Choose a System for Your Heavy-Industry Assets


Choose by your hardest assets first, then by service model. List the crushers, kilns, mills and large motors whose failure stops production, mark which sit in classified areas or out of network range, and drop any system that cannot meet those conditions on paper.


1. **Screen on conditions:** shock range for crushers, a slow-speed method for kiln rollers and mill trunnions, hazardous certificates for coal and fuel areas, and a network option for remote sites.
2. **Decide who reads the data:** AI diagnosis inside the platform, vendor analysts on a service contract, or software your own analysts configure. This choice drives cost and response time more than sensor price.
3. **Pilot across failure types:** one crusher, the kiln main drive, one mill gearbox and two large motors test shock, slow speed, gear mesh and electrical faults together.
4. **Judge the pilot on findings:** count alerts that named a fault your team confirmed at teardown or inspection, and how long each took to reach a planner.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Which condition monitoring technique works on slow-speed kilns and mill trunnions?


Slow bearings produce weak, low-frequency vibration, so standard velocity readings often show a defect late. Ultrasound can pick up friction and impacts earlier at low speed. Ask each vendor for the lowest shaft speed its method has been used on and for an example from a kiln or mill.


### Do condition monitoring sensors need ATEX or IECEx certification in a cement plant or mine?


Where the area is classified, yes. Coal mills, fuel handling, solvent storage and some dusty zones are often classified, while many crusher and conveyor areas are not. Check your site's area classification drawing, then ask for the certificate that matches the zone or division before you buy.


### Can wireless vibration sensors survive crusher vibration and dust?


They can if the shock range, mounting and sealing fit the asset. Look for an acceleration range that covers the impacts on your crusher bearings, a screwed or drill-and-tap mount instead of a magnet, and an IP67 or higher rating. Ask the vendor for installs on crushers or similar high-impact equipment.


### Do I need plant Wi-Fi for wireless condition monitoring?


It depends on the system. Some sensors send data to a gateway that needs Ethernet or Wi-Fi, others use a mesh network to a gateway, and some receivers use cellular LTE so the plant network is not involved. Remote crushers, quarries and kiln areas without coverage favor a cellular option like Tractian.


### How many assets should a heavy-industry condition monitoring pilot cover?


Pick assets that fail in different ways rather than many of one type, so a short pilot exercises impact loading, slow rotation, gear wear and motor electrical problems at the same time. Ask each vendor how many points it recommends for a pilot and what a finding on each asset type looks like in its software. Run it long enough for the system to learn normal operation and flag at least one real finding.
